articles.title: Fever facing offseason questions, uncertain futures for Kelsey Mitchell and Sophie Cunningham after playoff exit: 'We didn't meet that [championship] expectation'
articles.summary: Indiana was bounced by Las Vegas for the second straight postseason.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever's season came to an end at the hands of the Las Vegas Aces for the second straight season on Friday night.

Despite a fourth consecutive season with an improved record, the Fever have won only a single playoff round since 2016. As the team heads into the offseason, there are several questions that will need to be answered before Kelsey Mitchell, Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston and Co. can run it back for the 2027 season.

Mitchell's future is one of those questions. The four-time WNBA All-Star and 2026 scoring champion can become an unrestricted free agent and is unsure about what she will eventually decide.

"It's too early for me to really tell what I need to do," said Mitchell , who has spent her entire nine-year career with the Fever. She added that she has to be "selfish" about making the best decision for her and her family.

"I've obviously built a Fever family here … I guess TBD," Mitchell added while saying, "Heck yeah," when asked if she'd be fine staying with the franchise for the rest of her career.

General manager Amber Cox said Mitchell is a "major priority" in the offseason.

"Our goal is for her to be a Fever girl the rest of her career," Cox said.

Another potential Fever free agent is forward Sophie Cunningham. The 30-year-old finished her second year in Indiana by averaging 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 43 games.

Cox said the plan is try to re-sign Cunningham, who inked a one-year deal in April to return.

"Sophie is a really solid leader in the locker room and a great connector ... an important voice in the locker room when we need her. She's an unrestricted free agent, so we'll see where those conversations take us," said Cox, who noted that the off-court controversy involving Cunningham this season will not impact the team's decision to bring her back.

Will head coach Stephanie White could be one of the offseason changes? This was her second season leading the Fever, and Cox said areas that need improvement will be addressed in the offseason.

"I think the expectation is always championship. We didn't meet that expectation, but we're going to learn from it and we're going to grow. Steph's players know that she rides for them," Cox said of White's performance. "She has great relationships with them and just continues to build on that every time we are together. It comes back to that continuity and how you build together."

White expressed an eagerness to stay beyond this season.

"At the end of the day, it's their decision about whether I return or not," White said. "I'd love the opportunity. I love this franchise ... and I hope to continue to be the coach."

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham Calls Out A'ja Wilson For 'Double Standard' in Video, Tells WNBA Star to 'Grow Up'
articles.summary: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said she feels the WNBA applied a "double standard" by not disciplining Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson for an incident involving a fan during a first-round matchup between the Aces and Fever.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said she feels the WNBA applied a "double standard" by not disciplining Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson for an incident involving a fan during a first-round matchup between the Aces and Fever.

Cunningham was called for a foul on Wilson in the fourth quarter of the Fever's Game 2 win Tuesday, after which a fan stood and pointed at Wilson .

Wilson, who stepped forward to confront the fan as multiple Aces players ran over to pull her away, did not face any additional discipline past the technical foul she received on the play.

"She's like the LeBron James of our league, and so of course they're not going to suspend her... Something should have happened," Cunningham said on Saturday's episode of her podcast, the No Hesitation Show with Drew Hanlen. "The two people who came off the bench onto the court, that should have happened. I think there's definitely a double standard."

Cunningham added she didn't want Wilson to have been ejected from the game in part because she feels the Fever "would have gotten a lot of backlash from that."

"We yell from the rooftops that we want equality, that we want to be treated like the men, that we want all this stuff and we deserve all these things, and we do, we do deserve it," Cunningham said. "But if you're asking for all these fans to come— and you have new fans, who are real sports fans, and they come and do something that a sports fan would probably do if you're on the opposing team, and then you're going to go for him for just pointing, saying that you fouled? Grow up."

Cunningham also said she felt the Aces benefitted from an "A'ja whistle" after her Fever teammate Caitlin Clark seemingly hinted at criticism of the refereeing of the first-round series by previously reacting to a disparity in foul calls.

Wilson said after Game 2 she saw the fan's actions as "unacceptable" and had apologized to her teammates for taking the tech. She bounced back in Game 3 by scoring 36 points and 10 rebounds as the Aces eliminated the Fever.

She and the Aces have since advanced to the semifinals, where their series against the Golden State Valkyries tips off Sunday at 4 p.m. ET.

articles.title: La ley del ex impera en la victoria de La Laguna Tenerife ante el Unicaja de Txus Vidorreta
articles.standfirst: Marcelinho y Guy acaban con el conjunto malagueño en el reencuentro del técnico con su antiguo equipo
articles.summary: Marcelinho y Guy acaban con el conjunto malagueño en el reencuentro del técnico con su antiguo equipo
articles.body: El Unicaja y Vidorreta fueron víctimas de la ley del ex. La Laguna Tenerife fue mejor que los malagueños en el Martín Carpena para ganar un partido que se decidió al inicio del último cuarto (75-80), cuando el equipo insular encadenó un parcial de 0-10. Kendrick Perry fue el encargado de liderar el inicio ofensivo del Unicaja, mientras que La Laguna Tenerife encontró en el lanzamiento exterior una de sus principales vías de anotación. Los malagueños consiguieron mantener la iniciativa durante buena parte del primer periodo, aunque el conjunto visitante respondió cada vez que el Unicaja intentaba abrir diferencias. Una suspensión de Perry sobre la bocina permitió a los locales terminar por delante el primer cuarto (23-21). La igualdad se mantuvo durante el segundo periodo. La Laguna Tenerife tomó inicialmente la iniciativa, pero el Unicaja fue capaz de reaccionar gracias al acierto de Hunt y a la aportación de sus jugadores exteriores. Ambos equipos intercambiaron ventajas durante varios minutos en un partido con alternativas constantes. Pantzar y Noua volvieron a dar ventaja al conjunto malagueño, aunque el equipo visitante volvió a equilibrar el encuentro antes del descanso. Huertas, con una suspensión sobre la bocina, estableció el empate al término de la primera mitad (39-39). El Unicaja salió mejor tras el descanso y encontró en Brazdeikis una de sus principales referencias ofensivas. La Laguna Tenerife reaccionó rápidamente con Guy y Huertas al frente y volvió a tomar el control del partido. El encuentro continuó con alternativas y sin que ninguno de los dos equipos lograra establecer una diferencia definitiva. El conjunto insular llegó mejor al tramo final del periodo y terminó el tercer cuarto con ventaja (55-59). El inicio del último cuarto resultó determinante. La Laguna Tenerife aprovechó la falta de acierto del Unicaja para encadenar un parcial de 0-10 y abrir una diferencia importante. Los malagueños tardaron casi cuatro minutos y medio en volver a anotar, pero Kravish puso fin a la sequía y Noua contribuyó a reducir la distancia con varias acciones consecutivas. El Unicaja encontró entonces más acierto desde el perímetro y volvió a acercarse en el marcador. Perry asumió protagonismo en los últimos minutos y mantuvo a los locales con opciones de remontada. En el tramo final, el conjunto malagueño llegó a ponerse a una posesión, pero La Laguna Tenerife respondió con un palmeo de Abromaitis y, posteriormente, con dos tiros libres de Jaime Fernández. El Unicaja no pudo completar la remontada y La Laguna Tenerife se llevó la victoria del Martín Carpena por 75-80. 75- Unicaja (23+16+16+20): Perry (23), Hunt (13), Brazdeikis (4), Noua (13), Kravish (9) -quinteto inicial- Barreiro (5), Hernangómez (6), Djedovic (0), Lukosius (0), Pantzar (2), Thomas (0). 80- La Laguna Tenerife (21+18+20+21): Huertas (17), Guy (18), López-Arostegui (6), Abromaitis (7), Happ (8) -quinteto inicial- Fernández (13), Fitipaldo (0), Shermadini (0), Hunter (5), Alderete (0), Doornekamp (3), Kurucs (3). Árbitros: Carlos Peruga, Juan de Dios Oyón y David Sánchez. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la jornada 2 de la Liga Endesa, disputado en el Palacio de los Deportes José María Martín Carpena ante 9.936 espectadores. articles.title: What is latest on Marquette's Colin Porter getting a fifth season?
articles.summary: Colin Porter didn't play in Marquette's intrasquad scrimmage because his eligibility with the NCAA remains in limbo.
articles.body:
Marquette men's basketball fans are still waiting to get their first glimpse of Colin Porter.

Who knows if the transfer guard from Liberty will ever appear in a Golden Eagles uniform after suffering a setback in his legal quest for a fifth season of eligibility.

MU coach Shaka Smart held Porter out of the team's intrasquad scrimmage on Oct. 3, a day after the Kentucky Court of Appeals dissolved a temporary injunction in a lawsuit in which Porter and former Menomonee Falls standout Seth Trimble (now at Louisville) are among the plaintiffs.

That lawsuit is still pending. Porter's name is also attached to a similar lawsuit in North Carolina. Players from the class of 2022 recruiting class are seeking fifth seasons because the NCAA has allowed that for the classes that came after 2022.

"Colin is in limbo because of this fifth-year stuff," Smart said. "I guess there's stuff coming up this week with his case.

"So we're just kind of TBD with him, just trying to support him through it. He has been great. I feel bad for him that he's in limbo with this, but he's been awesome with his approach."

This a unique situation for a college basketball coach. It is under a month until MU's first game against Mercyhurst on Nov. 2 at Fiserv Forum.

"Colin is such a great kid," Smart said. "The first thing he said to me is 'I don't want to be a distraction for the team.'

"This was something that we knew when we took him that this could be up in the air, it could be in limbo. We had conversations with people in the NCAA that in this particular case are directly fighting against the fifth-year guys getting eligibility. We decided at that point that it made sense to try to do, but we knew that it wouldn't be 100%.

"Colin knew that as well. He has been phenomenal. Couldn't have been any better in the last five weeks since he's been here. Now our job is to just support the heck out of him. Obviously plan both ways. Prepare both ways, because he's somebody that would definitely make an impact on our team if he can play.

"But if he can't play, then we certainly need to plan for that scenario. Which in all honestly, he wasn't here all summer, so that was something we planning for in the first place."

articles.title: Kelsey Mitchell says she’ll be ‘selfish’ about future as Fever free agency looms
articles.summary: Questions about fan behavior, the Indiana Fever’s future and Kelsey Mitchell’s free agency dominated discussions as members of the Fever met with reporters f...
articles.body:
Questions about fan behavior, the Indiana Fever's future and Kelsey Mitchell's free agency dominated discussions as members of the Fever met with reporters following their playoff elimination.

Mitchell, who has only played in a Fever uniform during her nine WNBA seasons, said she would "be selfish about where my career is going" as an unrestricted free agent. She also discussed the challenges of playing in the spotlight as Caitlin Clark's teammate.

"I don't think people really understand how much we endure, man," said Mitchell, who ranked second in WNBA scoring and set single-game and 3-point records this season. "Like, if I showed y'all my DMs about the hate and all of the stuff that comes with being a professional athlete, but specifically being an Indiana Fever basketball player, it's a lot that goes into that. And those days are hard as hell, man.

"Playing with (Clark) and having the eyes that she's got (on her), we get a lot of flak just from being on her team."

Player-fan tensions have been mounting in the WNBA and were evident during the Fever's first-round playoff series against the Las Vegas Aces. In the Fever's 99-89 Game 2 win at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Tuesday, reigning MVP A'ja Wilson confronted a fan seated behind the baseline.

Fever general manager Amber Cox defended her team's fans in her exit interview Saturday, saying the "attacks on our fanbase have no basis in reality."

The man who pointed and yelled at Wilson was temporarily removed from his seat but was found to have not violated the fan code of conduct. (Wilson received a technical foul but no further repercussions from the league.) Similarly, in an August game, a fan Jewell Loyd identified to officials was also found to have not broken conduct rules.

"Here's the fact: We did not have one fan pointed out by a player who violated the WNBA code of conduct this season," Cox said. "Not one fan was removed from a game. … Our fans love this team. They're going to cheer, they're going to boo, and sometimes they might point. It's a home-court advantage for a reason, and it's the same for the Pacers. And all of that is within the code of conduct."

Cox said fans who cross the line — in arenas and online — should be held accountable.

Former Indiana forward Brianna Turner, who now plays with the Aces, disputed Cox's characterization of Fever fans.

"This is an unequivocally false statement," said Turner, an eight-year veteran who played 27 games for the Fever in 2025, on X. "Players inside and outside the organization have repeatedly issued complaints with the Fever fanbase. While it's not all Indy fans, it's certainly a trend. To say the attacks have 'no basis in reality' is disingenuous."

The Fever seem eager to keep Mitchell as part of a core with Clark and Aliyah Boston in hopes of becoming title contenders . Mitchell averaged 24.7 points this season and was an MVP contender.

Mitchell told reporters that she's built a "Fever family" in Indiana and that "everything I've grown to be is (because of) the Fever." Free agency begins in late January 2027. Mitchell said she hasn't thought deeply about her options yet so soon after her season ended.

Fever coach Stephanie White lauded her star backcourt's on-court chemistry on Thursday.

"(Mitchell and Clark) complement one another so well," White said. "They make each other better. They make each other's lives easier. They've just been a joy to coach."

articles.title: Trae Young Leaves Door Open for Future Hawks Reunion After Wizards Trade, 'You Never Know'
articles.summary: Even though Trae Young is still in the early stages of a new chapter with the Washington Wizards, he won't close the door on one day potentially returning to his original team.
articles.body:
Even though Trae Young is still in the early stages of a new chapter with the Washington Wizards, he won't close the door on one day potentially returning to his original team.

Appearing on The Baller Alert Show (starts at 12:40 mark), Young said "you never know" when asked if he would at some point consider playing for the Atlanta Hawks again.

"Man, you never know," Young said. "Like that's why the NBA is just such a… For me, I plan on playing for a long time . So, like I that's why I wanted to leave the right way, you know what I'm saying? And for me to not have any like bad blood with anybody in the city or any of the fans. (...) That's that's why I wanted to leave on the right terms. And sometimes breakups are meant to happen, but just how they go down is what's most important. But for me right now, obviously my 10 toes are here in DC. "

Young spent the first eight seasons of his career in Atlanta. He made the All-Star team four times and helped the franchise make three consecutive playoff appearances from 2021 to '23, including a trip to the Eastern Conference Finals in 2021.

After the Hawks didn't sign Young to a contract extension last offseason, it seemed to signal the possibility a split could be coming. The two sides eventually worked together on a trade to find a destination that would benefit him.

Young landed in Washington on Jan. 9 in exchange for CJ McCollum and Corey Kispert. His farewell message to Atlanta fans written on social media did not suggest there were any hard feelings toward the Hawks organization.

Injuries limited Young to just 15 games last season, including five with the Wizards after the deal. Despite his lack of playing time in 2025-26, he secured a four-year, $212 million contract from Washington in free agency.

The Wizards have a fascinating roster going into this season. Young, Anthony Davis, AJ Dybantsa, Alex Sarr and Bub Carrington is an interesting group of five.

Dybantsa's development is the most important thing for Washington, but keeping Young and Davis healthy will go a long way toward determining if this is a playoff team in the East.

Given how popular and important Young was for Atlanta basketball during his time there, it's not a surprise he isn't ruling out a reunion down the line.

For now, though, the Wizards will be hoping to get the best version of Young as they try to take a step forward coming off three consecutive seasons with fewer than 20 wins.

articles.body: Un Río Breogán liderado por Dominik Mavra (22 puntos, 10 asistencias y 35 de valoración) y que fue de menos a más, venció con claridad a un Kids&Us Manresa intermitente y desacertado a lo largo de los cuarenta minutos (95-101). A pesar de que los locales realizaron un gran inicio de encuentro y llegaron a mandar por once puntos, el cuadro gallego acumuló progresivamente buenas sensaciones a ambos lados de la pista y se convirtió en una apisonadora, alcanzando los veintidós tantos de diferencia. Además, se ha convertido en el primer equipo en anotar más de cien puntos en las dos primeras jornadas de la liga desde 2004. A la buena actuación de Mavra se sumaron los 17 puntos, 5 rebotes, 5 asistencias y 21 créditos de valoración de Tevin Brown. Por parte del Manresa, Timmy Allen completó una actuación espectacular (30 puntos, 8 rebotes y 35 de valoración), aunque no obtuvo el premio del triunfo para su equipo. Los del Bages, liderados por un gran Rafa Villar (cinco puntos y un tapón en el primer período), iniciaron el partido con una marcha más que los lucenses y lograron situar la primera ventaja de la noche con un parcial de salida 14-3 en apenas dos minutos que obligó al técnico visitante, Luis Casimiro, a pedir el primer tiempo muerto del duelo. Poco a poco, el Breogán se fue encontrando en ataque, pero los locales siguieron intratables de cara al aro y mantuvieron la renta durante varios minutos (21-7, min.5). Sin embargo, un parcial 6-17 de los visitantes en el tramo final del cuarto rebajó la diferencia a tan solo tres tantos (27-24, min.10). En el segundo cuarto, el encuentro entró en una fase de imprecisiones y excesivas pérdidas por parte de ambos conjuntos, una circunstancia que se vio reflejada en la baja anotación durante los primeros cuatro minutos, en los que únicamente se anotó un triple por parte del Manresa y una canasta de dos puntos en el cuadro gallego. Con el paso de los segundos, el conjunto celeste mejoró sus porcentajes y consiguió situarse por delante en el marcador por primera vez en el encuentro, provocando que Diego Ocampo pidiera tiempo muerto hasta en dos ocasiones (34-41, min.17). Los locales no reaccionaron, y ello lo aprovecharon los visitantes, guiados por Dominik Mavra (15 puntos y 8 asistencias en la primera mitad), para aumentar la diferencia antes del paso por vestuarios y completar un parcial 13-27 (40-51, min.20). Tras el descanso, el guión del partido no varió. El Breogán estaba de dulce en ataque y centrado en defensa, y un mate de Tevin Brown estableció una nueva máxima renta para los suyos (46-68, min.24). No obstante, el Kids&Us Manresa no arrojó la toalla. Gracias a una sustancial mejora en los porcentajes desde el perímetro, encadenaron ocho puntos seguidos que obligaron a parar el partido a Casimiro tan solo un minuto más tarde. La ventaja se estabilizó, y el tercer período prosiguió con un largo intercambio de golpes entre ambos equipos en el que ninguno de ellos consiguió romper el marcador. Un arreón final de los visitantes volvió a situar la máxima diferencia tras un triple de Rasir Bolton (67-89, min.30). Al inicio del último cuarto, el conjunto del Bages recibió un nuevo mazazo después de que Nick Ongenda fuera expulsado por cinco faltas personales. No obstante, sin uno de los principales recursos sobre la pista, los de Diego Ocampo fueron capaces de meter algo de miedo a los lucenses (81-94, min.37). Sin embargo, el Río Breogán supo gestionar los instantes finales e impidió que el cuadro local materializara el intento de remontada (95-101). 95 - Kids&Us Manresa (27+13+27+12): Allen (30), Agbo (14), Notae (20), Ongenda (7), Villar (7) -cinco inicial- Kolenda (7), Vila (-), Beaufort (3), Bassas (-), Tamba (6), Enabuele (-) y Minchev (1). 101 - Río Breogán (24+27+38+12): Brown (17), Peris (3), Brankovic (9), Andric (2), Bolton (13) -cinco inicial- Ilic (4), Alonso (13), García (7), Aranitovic (7), Mavra (22) y Kasibabu (4). Árbitros: Fernando Calatrava, Sergio Manuel y Rubén Sánchez Mohedas. Eliminaron a Ongenda y Allen (Kids&Us Manresa) por cinco faltas personales. articles.title: La mejor noticia en la marejada del Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Maledon es el base que mejor y más rápido se ha adaptado al baloncesto de Pedro Martínez: líder de los blancos en puntos, asistencias y valoración
articles.summary: Maledon es el base que mejor y más rápido se ha adaptado al baloncesto de Pedro Martínez: líder de los blancos en puntos, asistencias y valoración
articles.body: En el irregular comienzo de temporada del Real Madrid se puede encontrar una buena noticia. Es el rendimiento de Theo Maledon. El francés es el base que antes y mejor ha encajado en la filosofía de baloncesto de Pedro Martínez, bastante por delante de Facundo Campazzo y Andrés Feliz. Tras un primer curso algo gris para lo que se esperaba de él, ha dado un paso adelante en sus prestaciones y en las sensaciones que ofrece en la pista. “Siento que me estoy adaptando más. Estoy empezando a entender mejor el sistema y a encontrar formas de impactar en el juego en ambos lados de la cancha, no sólo en ataque, sino cumpliendo con lo que se requiere en defensa. Para mí está siendo una experiencia de aprendizaje para intentar seguir adelante con esa confianza”, decía antes de la doble jornada de Euroliga de esta semana, donde ha lucido. Maledon se está manteniendo firme en la marejada que vive el Madrid con esas tres derrotas seguidas para comenzar la Euroliga, que ya son el peor arranque del club en la historia de la competición. Suerte que el triunfo en la novedosa SuperCup ya haya asegurado un título y esté amortiguando los tropiezos recientes. Pese a las derrotas, el base ha demostrado su crecimiento. Tras la SuperCup, ha sido el máximo anotador y el jugador más valorado del conjunto madridista en tres de los cuatro encuentros. En la Euroliga es el segundo que más juega sólo por detrás de Edy Tavares (22:48 minutos), promedia 15,3 puntos, 6,0 asistencias y 22,7 créditos de valoración. Es el quinto mejor de la competición en esta última estadística. Este domingo, se plantará en Santiago para enfrentarse al recién ascendido Monbus Obradoiro (12.30 horas) después de haber firmado la mejor actuación de su carrera en la Euroliga. Este jueves, en la derrota ante el Hapoel Tel Aviv, hizo 26 puntos, cinco rebotes, siete asistencias y 40 de valoración. Frente al Unicaja, en la única jornada disputada en la Liga Endesa, acabó con 17 puntos, a uno de su mejor registro en ACB, y 23 de valoración, a tres de su tope. “La temporada es larga, pero lo importante es ser constante”, asegura un Maledon que ha trabajado mucho en el gimnasio este verano. Ha ganado tanto músculo como madurez en la pista. Su toma de decisiones parece mejor que hace un año mientras sigue siendo un cuchillo atravesando la zona rival y su facilidad para forzar tiros libres es oxígeno para los momentos de atasco. Su lunar, el triple. Si fuera más fiable, quizás no habría dejado la NBA.

articles.title: Fever's Kelsey Mitchell Says She'll Be 'Selfish' with Decision in 2026 WNBA Free Agency
articles.summary: Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell is prioritizing herself as she prepares to hit free agency.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell is prioritizing herself as she prepares to hit free agency.

"I have to be selfish," Mitchell said Saturday, per ESPN's Kareem Copeland . "I think that's where I am in my career ... what I probably need and what's probably best for me. So I have to be selfish in that room.

"But I think, ultimately, being on the Fever and being a part of an organization that does come with a lot of ups and downs, what factors in and what is important for me is, obviously, having a good chemistry on and off the floor. I've only been with one team my entire career, so it's all kind of like figuring this out. It's hard, man."

Indiana's 2026 season came to an end after it was eliminated by the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the playoffs on Thursday night.

The Fever are now preparing to navigate through the offseason, with Mitchell set to become a free agent.

She's spent all nine years of her career as a member of the organization after Indiana selected her with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2018 WNBA draft. Mitchell has blossomed into a top offensive option for the Fever, earning All-Star nods in each of her past four seasons.

In 2026, the 30-year-old ranked No. 2 in the league with her scoring average of 24.7 points per game. She also recorded 2.8 assists, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 steals on a nightly basis while shooting a career-high 50.9 percent from the field and 45.0 percent from three-point territory.

The Fever owned a plus-8.7 net rating with Mitchell on the court during the regular season compared to a minus-0.1 net rating with her off the floor (via WNBA.com ).

As Indiana looks to build around its young duo of Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston in order to contend for a fourth consecutive playoff berth in 2027, the future of Mitchell is something to monitor.

articles.title: Giannis Makes Heat Preseason Debut After Bucks Trade, Final Box Score Stats & Highlights
articles.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo made his preseason debut for the Miami Heat on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo made his preseason debut for the Miami Heat on Saturday night.

Antetokounmpo played 14 minutes in the first half of Miami's clash with the Toronto Raptors in Québec City after the Heat acquired him in a blockbuster trade with the Milwaukee Bucks on June 22.

Here's a closer look at how he fared through two quarters.

Antetokounmpo didn't appear to have any issue building chemistry with his new teammates, as he routinely kicked the ball out to open shooters after drawing extra defensive attention inside the arc.

His seven assists came against just two turnovers.

Antetokounmpo showcased his efficient scoring ability around the rim while also expanding his range, connecting on a one-legged fadeaway.

The Heat are coming off a 2025-26 campaign in which they missed the playoffs with a 43-39 record, but are looking to climb up the Eastern Conference standings with the two-time MVP in the mix.

Antetokounmpo appeared in 36 contests last season, averaging 27.6 points, 9.8 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 0.9 steals per game while shooting 62.4 percent from the field and 33.3 percent from three-point territory.

The Heat will open the 2026-27 regular season against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo posts 9 points, 7 assists in first Heat appearance, rests second half
articles.summary: Antetokounmpo rested in the second half, along with the other Miami starters.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat took on the Toronto Raptors in Québec City on Saturday night. While it marked the start of NBA preseason, it also marked star forward Giannis Antetokounmpo's first game appearance with his new team.

He played only the first half of Miami's 129-105 preseason blowout win, but that limited action was enough to affect the game and show how the Heat could use him on offense this season.

Antetokounmpo didn't score Miami's first points. Andrew Wiggins got the honor, nailing a 3 off a pass from Antetokounmpo. This became a common play for the Heat: the star forward barrels down the lane, then kicks out to the arc for a teammate to hit a 3.

The forward scored his first points with Miami on a layup early in the first quarter, and converted the and-one.

New team? Same fadeaway. Antetokounmpo made sure to pack his smooth jumper on the road trip.

The Miami forward finished the game with 9 points, 4 rebounds and 7 assists. Antetokounmpo shot a perfect 3-for-3 from the field but didn't attempt a 3-pointer. He also went 3-for-4 from the charity stripe.

The forward played 14 minutes in the first half and nearly had a double-double. With Miami up 20 through the first two quarters, the Heat rested their starters for the second half.

Antetokounmpo seemed to debut a new pre-game ritual. It will be interesting to see if he continues this in Miami or during the regular season. It is similar to the sprint that Russell Westbrook used to do down the court ahead of the action, with "The Greek Freak's" added flair.

Antetokounmpo finally got the trade he wanted this past summer as the Milwaukee Bucks sent him and Bobby Portis to Miami for Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakučionis and five draft picks.

Saturday night's win over Toronto was the first of five preseason games the Heat will play. Miami will face the New Orleans Pelicans, Minnesota Timberwolves, Brooklyn Nets and Orlando Magic before beginning the regular season at home against Minnesota on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

articles.title: NBA trade rumor: Lakers could add 6-foot-6 Luka Doncic ex-teammate and Clippers forward as final roster piece
articles.summary: The Lakers overhauled their roster this summer, and one starting spot still looks unfinished.
articles.body: The Lakers overhauled their roster this summer, and one starting spot still looks unfinished. Walker Kessler and Quentin Grimes arrived, while LeBron James, Marcus Smart and Deandre Ayton left. Lakers need perimeter defense, secondary rim protection and enough offense to hold up. No one on the roster fits it as a proven power forward, and that probably doesn't change before opening night.Derrick Jones Jr. keeps coming up as the fix. The 6-foot-6 Clippers forward, 29, played one season beside Luka Doncic in Dallas, and a Clippers roster stripped of five first-round picks might listen. Reports published October 3 put him forward as an option. Nothing is agreed, and every idea here is speculation, not word from either front office.CategoryDetailsPlayerDerrick Jones Jr. (forward, 6-foot-6, 29)Current TeamLos Angeles ClippersRumored TeamLos Angeles LakersContract StatusFinal year; extension not expectedTrade LikelihoodSpeculative; Clippers' asking price unclearLatest Insider UpdateOct. 3: Lakers-Clippers deal proposed; asking price unclearPotential ReturnLaRavia, and three second-round picks to the Clippers (hypothetical)Why are the Lakers targeting Derrick Jones Jr.?Los Angeles has two in-house candidates in newcomers Ziaire Williams and Sandro Mamukelashvili, and either could claim the starting power forward job. Right now, it is fair to say that the newcomer duo is a backup option or a trade asset. Jones would upgrade any in-house option as a proven, veteran two-way contributor. His strength, agility and verticality suit a defender beside Doncic, who can feed him enough quality shots to stay viable on offense.What insiders are saying about the trade?As the summer roster changes happened, it looks like the Lakers are reaching the end of perfecting their team. Still, there are some gaps. "The Lakers need a forward and the Los Angeles Clippers need some draft capital, which makes these two teams the perfect trading partners," Fansided’s Mat Issa wrote. "This one would be another reunion for Dončić from his Finals run with the Dallas Mavericks. Here, the Lakers would trade LaRavia, Dalton Knecht and three second-round picks to get Derrick Jones Jr."Derrick Jones Jr.'s expiring deal and the Clippers' five lost first-roundersJones is in the final year of his contract and is not expected to get an extension. The league docked the Clippers five first-round picks, and the forward is believed to be among the veterans on their trade block. Moving him before the deadline would return something, while waiting risks losing him for nothing. Los Angeles could also hang back and wait for Jones to test free agency next summer. The Clippers' asking price is unclear.P.J. Washington in Dallas and Herbert Jones in New Orleans are other names on the radar, and Washington looks like the surer option.Doncic, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler and Quentin Grimes already project as four starters, with one spot open. The clock runs in two directions. Los Angeles will judge Williams and Mamukelashvili over roughly two months, and the Clippers face the trade deadline with an expiring contract. If neither Laker claims the spot, the calls start. If the Clippers sit still, Jones may walk next summer with no return. articles.standfirst: El iLERNA Lleida celebraba el 25 aniversario de la inauguración de su pabellón
articles.summary: El iLERNA Lleida celebraba el 25 aniversario de la inauguración de su pabellón
articles.body: El Recoletas San Pablo Burgos sumó su primera victoria en la Liga Endesa al vencer al iLerna Lleida por 81-94 en un choque que no se decidió hasta el los instantes finales. En el 25 aniversario de la inauguración del Barris Nord, los catalanes desplegaron un gran juego, pero se vieron lastrados por los malos porcentajes (20% desde el perímetro). Por su parte, el Burgos fue de menos a más a lo largo del choque y estuvo acertado cuando más quemaba el balón. Dj Seward y Chase Audige, ambos con 20 puntos, fueron los líderes de los burgaleses en ataque. En el bando ilerdense, James Batemon fue un día más el más destacado del equipo burdeos (16 puntos, 3 rebotes y 4 asistencias). Ambos equipos comenzaron el partido un tanto erráticos en ataque y cometieron varias pérdidas, lo que propició un juego con mucho ritmo y posesiones (7-6, min. 5). Con la llegada de las primeras rotaciones, ninguno de los dos conjuntos fue capaz de mejorar sus registros en ataque. Los visitantes optaron por dar un poco de pausa a sus posesiones, mientras que los locales siguieron fieles a su juego dinámico y consiguieron sumar puntos desde la línea de tiro libre (20-19, min.10). En el segundo período, el Lleida se fue encontrando en ataque y situó, tras un contraataque culminado por Melvin Ejim, una renta de seis puntos, la máxima hasta entonces, que obligó a Porfirio Fisac a pedir el primer tiempo muerto del encuentro (34-28, min.16). Poco a poco, los castellanos reaccionaron y, sin encadenar un gran parcial, lograron rebajar la diferencia a un tan solo punto, obligando a Gerard Encuentra a pedir tiempo muerto (40-39, min.19). El Lleida, que hoy vestía con su equipación azul en homenaje a el Caprabo Lleida que inauguró el Barris Nord, se arremangó en defensa y gozó de tiros liberados para ampliar la diferencia en los últimos minutos de la primera mitad, pero solo logró anotar un punto. De este modo, el choque se fue a vestuarios con 41-39 en el electrónico. Tras el descanso, el Lleida empezó a ofuscarse en ataque, algo que aprovecharon los de Fiscac, más regulares sobre la pista, para dar la vuelta al partido y llevar la iniciativa en el luminoso por primera vez desde el inicio del segundo cuarto (52-56, min.29). Una canasta de Batemon estableció el 54-56 con el que el duelo llegó al último período. Cuando más dudas tenían los locales, la dupla Batemon-McGhee cogió las riendas del equipo, que firmó un parcial 6-0 de salida que enloqueció al Barris Nord (60-56, min. 31). El choque entró en una fase de alternancias en el marcador en la que brilló especialmente Chase Audige, quien convirtió los primeros ocho puntos de su equipo en el período y catapultó a los suyos cinco arriba (62-67, min.35). A pesar de que el iLerna Lleida mantuvo vivas hasta el final las opciones de culminar la remontada, un triple errado por McGhee a falta de menos de un minuto para el final prácticamente sentenció el choque (77-84, min 39). En los últimos instantes, los catalanes encadenaron varios despropósitos en ataque que permitieron a los burgaleses situar el 81-92 final, un resultado que no refleja la igualdad durante los cuarenta minutos. 81 - iLerna Lleida (20+21+13+27): McGhee (3), Ejim (15), Paulí (8), Hughes (3), Perrin (17) -cinco inicial- Batemon (16), García (6), Rodríguez (-), Sanz (3), Shurna (2) y Kuath (8). 94 - Recoletas Salud San Pablo Burgos (19+20+17+38): Steward (20), Koprivica (13), Radosavljevic (2), Sengfelder (11), Lobaco (-) -cinco inicial- Audige (20), Samar (14), Almazán (-), Díez (3), Doumbuya (11) y Taboada (-). Árbitros: Martín Caballero, Javier Torres y Vicente Martínez. articles.title: El Carpena se llena para disfrutar de los Cavaliers de Harden
articles.standfirst: 10.000 personas ven en directo la exhibición del equipo de Cleveland
articles.summary: 10.000 personas ven en directo la exhibición del equipo de Cleveland
articles.body: El 4 de octubre de 2026 quedará señalado como una fecha especial para el baloncesto malagueño. También con argumentos para ocupar un lugar destacado en el panorama nacional. Los Cleveland Cavaliers pusieron el punto final a su training camp en Málaga con un scrimmage abierto al público que llevó a cerca de 10.000 aficionados al Martín Carpena. La expectación fue creciendo desde mucho antes de que comenzara el partido. Casi dos horas antes del salto inicial ya había aficionados en las gradas buscando el mejor sitio posible. Las localidades no estaban numeradas y eso convirtió los accesos al pabellón en una particular carrera por conseguir una buena ubicación para ver de cerca a las estrellas de los Cavs. Y el cartel invitaba a ello. El público malagueño pudo disfrutar sobre la pista de nombres como James Harden, Donovan Mitchell o Mario Hezonja, en una jornada poco habitual para la ciudad. El encuentro también contó con una importante representación del deporte malagueño. El Unicaja tuvo una presencia destacada en la zona VIP, con Txus Vidorreta, Fede Van Lacke —integrante del cuerpo técnico del entrenador bilbaíno— y jugadores como Kendrick Perry, David Hunt, Yannick Nzosa o Melvin Kalinoski siguiendo el partido a pie de pista. También hubo representación del Málaga CF. Joaquín Muñoz y Adrián Niño aprovecharon su jornada de descanso para acercarse al Carpena y presenciar en directo el entrenamiento de los Cavaliers. Ambos ya habían coincidido con el equipo de la NBA el viernes en The Embassy, donde asistieron a una de las sesiones dirigidas por Kenny Atkinson. El scrimmage tuvo desde el comienzo algunos momentos especialmente celebrados por el público. James Harden fue el encargado de inaugurar el marcador con un triple, una de las acciones que más ruido generó en las gradas del Carpena. Pero si hubo un jugador que buscó asumir responsabilidades fue Mario Hezonja. El croata se mostró especialmente participativo, pidió balón constantemente y tuvo un importante peso ofensivo durante el partido. No es casualidad. Hezonja se juega mucho durante estas semanas en Cleveland. Su contrato no tiene garantizada su continuidad y los Cavaliers podrían prescindir de sus servicios antes del 15 de noviembre. Por eso, cada entrenamiento y cada partido de preparación cuenta. El escenario, además, abre otras posibilidades. En el entorno del jugador no descartan que su aventura en Cleveland pueda terminar convirtiéndose en un puente hacia Europa. Dubái aparece como uno de los destinos mejor posicionados en caso de un regreso a la Euroliga, especialmente teniendo en cuenta el mercado de jugadores que maneja su representante, Misko Raznatovic. Pero eso pertenece todavía al terreno de las posibilidades. El tiempo será el encargado de determinar si Hezonja continúa en la NBA o si su paso por los Cavaliers termina siendo una escala antes de regresar al baloncesto europeo.

articles.standfirst: El conjunto blanquiazul visita al cuadro de la NBA en Fuengirola
articles.summary: El conjunto blanquiazul visita al cuadro de la NBA en Fuengirola
articles.body: Los jugadores del Málaga CF Joaquín Muñoz, Fernando Calero y Adrián Niño aprovecharon este viernes su primer día libre del fin de semana para acercarse hasta The Embassy, en Fuengirola, y presenciar en directo el entrenamiento de los Cleveland Cavaliers. El equipo de la NBA continúa con su preparación en la Costa del Sol antes del inicio de la temporada regular. Los tres futbolistas blanquiazules pudieron seguir de cerca la tercera sesión de los Cavaliers en tierras malagueñas, con estrellas como James Harden, Mario Hezonja o Donovan Mitchell sobre la pista. El conjunto estadounidense aterrizó en Málaga el pasado martes y, tras una primera jornada marcada por la aclimatación y el cambio horario, comenzó a entrenarse el miércoles. La visita de los malaguistas se produce durante el primero de los tres días de descanso concedidos por Funes a la plantilla. El Málaga disputó el jueves un partido de entrenamiento ante el Córdoba CF y no regresará al trabajo hasta el lunes 5 de octubre, cuando empezará a preparar ya su próximo compromiso liguero. El siguiente partido será el viernes 9 de octubre, a las 21:00 horas, ante el RCD Espanyol en La Rosaleda. Será el regreso de la competición para el conjunto de Funes después del parón por selecciones y de dos semanas sin jornada de LaLiga.

articles.body: Volvía la ACB a La Coruña después del descenso hace un año y recibía el Leyma a un Bilbao Basket con muy buenas sensaciones. Derrota en el Palau pero compitiendo tres cuartos y por parte visitante victoria cómoda ante Manresa. El primer cuarto estuvo muy igualado con ventajas siempre controladas por el rival. La máxima de Leyma (22-16) a escasos segundos del final. Los dos center de ambos equipos los máximos anotadores Skapintsev, seis puntos y Hlinason, ocho. Precisamente el pivot islandés estaba muy fino en ataque y la defensa coruñesa no lograba pararlo (doce puntos en los dos primeros cuartos). Sorprendía que la estrella de los vascos Hilliard no logró anotar en el primer cuarto y estrenaba su casillero con dos triples a dos minutos del descanso. Las rotaciones eran constantes en ambas plantillas. Y la igualdad era total en los dos primeros cuartos (46-45). El partido se reanudó con un Harald Frey enchufadísimo. Dos trilples y una asistencia del noruego en los primeros minutos colocaba por primera vez por delante a los visitantes (57-59) a falta de cuatro minutos para el final del cuarto. Pero el Coliseum apretaba y gracias a un triple de Pacheco empataba el choque (60-60). Seguía la igualdad máxima y a un minuto del final del tercer cuarto el marcador era de empate (67-67) El último cuarto las defensas estaban siendo muy buenas por ambos equipos. Pero apareció en escena un gran Alonzo Verge máximo anotador del encuentro (29). Un triple suyo ponía la máxima ventaja (86-79) a falta de tres minutos. A falta de 1:43 un choque cabeza con cabeza entre Radoncic y Hlimason y ambos tuvieron que abandonar el encuentro con sendas brechas y abundante sangre. Los últimos tres minutos fueron frenéticos. Un gran Surne Bilbao liderados por Frey, Darling y sobre todo un inmenso Hilliard que anotó el triple que forzaba el tiempo extra. Los vascos remontaron nueve puntos en dos minutos. Comenzó con sendos triples por ambos equipos Alonzo y Normantas los protagonistas. Los tiros libres estaban siendo claves con ambos equipos en bonus… visitaron la línea Pacheco, Normantas, Skapintsev, Petrasek… Se llegó al final del partido con tres arriba el Leyma (104-101) y la posibilidad de otra prórroga si anotaba el triple Bilbao pero Vautier falló sin oposición. 104.- Básquet Coruña (22+24+23+22+13): Alonzo Verge (29), Jorgensen (9), Uleckas (14), George Conditt (6) y Silins (5) -cinco inicial- Guillem Jou (2), Radoncic (6), Caio Pacheco (13), Dmytro Skapintsev (12), Jacobo Díaz (4) y Cuevas (4). 101.- Surne Bilbao Basket (18+27+22+24+10): Frey (13), Normantas (16), Hilliard (17), Petrasek (11) y Hlinason (10) -cinco inicial- Krampelj (9), Vautier (3), Darling (12), Font (2) y Somogyi (8). articles.title: Maledon y Luwawu-Cabarrot evitan otro disgusto al Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: El base (25+3+7) y el alero (25+4) comandan el sufrido triunfo blanco en la prórroga ante un gran Monbus Obradoiro
articles.summary: El base (25+3+7) y el alero (25+4) comandan el sufrido triunfo blanco en la prórroga ante un gran Monbus Obradoiro
articles.body: Le tocó sufrir al Real Madrid para mantener su pleno de victorias en la recién estrenada competición liguera (107-114). Los siete puntos de diferencia final no reflejan el calvario que tuvo que padecer el cuadro de Pedro Martínez para sacar adelante un encuentro que el incansable Monbus Obradoiro había llevado a la prórroga. Maledon, con 38 créditos de valoración, y Luwawu-Cabarrot, con la pertinente ayuda de Pradilla y Jantunen, impidieron que la sublevación de los anfitriones, liderados por Childress y Soriano, hiciera saltar la sorpresa de la jornada. Era previsible, pero el Real Madrid vio equilibrado su talento y calidad individual con un ejercicio de intensidad del conjunto santiagués, pletórico de energía y con muchas ayudas en defensa. Los pupilos de Epi cerraron bastante bien su aro y obligaron al conjunto madridista, que apostó por mucho juego interior en el inicio, a asistir en muchas ocasiones, hasta 16 en el primer cuarto, a la línea de personales. Así fue como el elenco de Pedro Martínez fue equilibrando un partido que deslumbró con un inspirado Childress, una de las revelaciones del arranque liguero, haciéndose notar con cinco puntos seguidos que situaron la máxima ventaja de los anfitriones en el tanteador (7-1). Meindl, Barcello y un Agada que mostró las costuras de Okeke en un 2+1 prolongaron el buen momento del cuadro compostelano. El Real Madrid fue recortando diferencias con los puntos desde la línea de 4,60 como principal argumento. Así llegó la mitad de los 22 anotados en el primer cuarto, con Pradilla como principal ejecutor. La implicación de Maledon para hacer que pasaran cosas y un mate de Procida destacaron en la reacción de los hombres de Pedro Martínez, que llegaron a ponerse por delante (15-18), aunque las tablas imperaron al final del primer acto. Volvió a aparecer Childress con descaro en un segundo cuarto en el que el Madrid, que llegó a ganar por cinco puntos en varios tramos, empezó a marcar territorio, más aplicado en defensa, con un Tavares activo en ambas zonas. Un pase de fantasía de Childress con mate de Dos Anjos encendió la Caldera de Sar. Maledon también exhibió su destreza en las penetraciones y para desarmar defensas. Otro vuelo sin motor de Procida hizo recapacitar a Epi tras un 0-6 después de un tiempo muerto de Pedro Martínez (33-40). Otro triple de Maledon hizo que las instrucciones del técnico burgalés quedaran minimizadas. A la fiesta se sumaron Luwawu-Cabarrot y Jantunen, que anotó cinco puntos seguidos, y la diferencia al descanso comenzó a inquietar a la hinchada local (43-55). Barcello, con ocho puntos, reactivó en el tercer cuarto al Obra, más agresivo en las ayudas defensivas, y el técnico del Real Madrid tuvo que frenar la reacción de las huestes de Epi con un tiempo muerto (57-61). En pleno apagón visitante, sin un triple que echarse a la boca, Meindl y Barrueta equilibraron el tanteador (61-61). Okeke, desde fuera del arco, y Jantunen sacaron del atolladero al Madrid, que volvió a abrir otra brecha de once puntos. Pero si hay un equipo inasequible al desaliento ese es el Monbus Obradoiro, con una capacidad de resiliencia encomiable. Volvió a ponerse a cinco puntos, tras un triple de Agada, pero Smith y Luwawu-Cabarrot, bajo la tutela de Maledon, sofocaron la enésima revuelta del conjunto santiagués. No fue la última. Con más vidas que la pandilla de Don Gato, el Obradoiro volvió a empatar el duelo tras un triple de Sergi Quintela y un mate de un imperial Soriano, que propició un 2+1 y cerró un 11-0 de parcial (88-88). Incluso volvió a mandar la formación de Epi en el marcador, sin contar que Luwawu-Cabarrot rara vez perdona. Compensó su mala hoja de servicios inicial, con cuatro triples fallados, con cinco plenos seguidos y una incidencia decisiva en el juego. Pero Barrueta también reclamó protagonismo y su triple convenció al Madrid de que 40 minutos en Sar son siempre “molto longo” (96-94). Tan largos que hasta tuvieron ampliación. Porque Childress, que había encadenado un error en el tiro y una falta, enchufó un triple lejano que situó el empate a 99 con 16 segundos por delante. Marró Maledon y el encuentro entró en la prórroga. Pradilla y Maledon parecieron enterrar de nuevo al Obradoiro. Ni con el ataúd cerrado y con remaches se puede dar por muerto al conjunto santiagués, que entró por delante en el minuto final (105-104). Los tiros libres de Maledon voltearon la situación y Barrueta mandó al tablero el triple que podría haber llevado el encuentro a la segunda prórroga. 107.- Monbus Obradoiro (22+21+26+30+8): Childress (23), Brito (4), Leo Meindl (9), Alejandro Galán (2) y Joel Soriano (13) -cinco inicial-; Agada (16), Abogidi (-), Sergi Quintela (5), Dos Anjos (9), Barrueta (13) y Barcello (13). 114.- Real Madrid (22+32+21+24+15): Feliz (6), Luwawu-Cabarrot (25), Llull (2), Pradilla (8) y Tavares (8) -cinco inicial-; Maledon (25), Shulga (3), Okeke (8), Procida (6), Jantunen (13), Nick Smith (10) y Sarr (-). Árbitros: Alfonso Olivares, Alberto Sánchez Sixto e Igor Esteve. articles.title: Fever star Sophie Cunningham tells Aces' A'ja Wilson to 'grow up' in response to her playoff meltdown
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham blasted A'ja Wilson on her "No Hesitation" podcast for confronting a Fever fan who was simply pointing during the WNBA playoffs.
articles.body: If you know anything about Indiana Fever forward Sophie Cunningham, you know she's not going to mince words. She famously stated, "I said what I said," while speaking to the media following relentless backlash for saying men should not compete in women's sports. That’s why it shouldn’t shock anyone that Cunningham went off on WNBA MVP and Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson for confronting a Fever fan and verbally berating him in Game 2 at Gainbridge Fieldhouse for simply pointing at her. In the latest episode of "No Hesitation," hosted by Cunningham and elite basketball trainer Drew Hanlen, the Fever forward gave her long-awaited take on the now-infamous incident involving the controversial blocking call. "Oh my God! I have so many thoughts," Cunningham stated after her and Hanlen watched a clip from the "Pat McAfee Show" where one of the hosts (Boston Connor) confirmed, just as I did in my reporting following the incident, that the fan said, "It (the foul) is on you," while pointing. CRAIG CARTON BLASTS WNBA, A'JA WILSON OVER FAN CONFRONTATION: 'THIS LEAGUE CAN'T GET OUT OF ITS OWN WAY' While explaining that she held back from giving her reaction to the incident on X and saving it "for the pod," Cunningham went off on Wilson. "Us women in sport, and I'm just gonna say women in sport because that's my occupation and I have lived this, we yell from the rooftops that we want equality. We want to be treated like the men," she stated, prefacing her blunt comments. "We're gonna go for them for just pointing and saying, 'You fouled!'? Like grow up! What are we doing?" Cunningham said. She also took exception to the idea that Wilson, and seemingly other players, should be allowed to attack fans, claiming, "Us athletes need to be treated better" and "These fans need to be more supportive and not say anything negative." Cunningham pointed out that she has a unique perspective on this as one of the most, if not the most, hated WNBA players simply because she doesn’t believe men should be in women's sports and spaces. "I can say this, because I, hands down, have probably got s--- on the entire season, maybe sometimes two seasons — people coming after who I am, my character, what I stand for, x, y, z, I could go on and on." WHO IS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM? FOX NATION CHRONICLES THE WNBA STAR'S RISE FROM FARM GIRL TO WOMEN'S SPORTS ADVOCATE "I've heard the worst of the worst. It's part of it," Cunningham said. "You should be grateful to be on this platform. You should be grateful to be playing basketball for a living and inspiring the next generation. If you really want sports fans, then you're gonna get sports fans. That includes pointing. That includes getting yelled at. Probably [will] be getting called names." "I don't think [the Fever fan] did absolutely anything wrong," Cunningham said definitively. Maybe Cunningham's most controversial take was saying, "If you want to get technical, that (Wilson's actions) could've called for a suspension, but she's like the LeBron James of our league so of course they're (WNBA) not going to suspend her." Not only was Wilson not suspended, she was neither ejected, nor was she fined for her actions. Cunningham seems to say players of Wilson's caliber will be treated far less harshly and get away with clear violations. Cunningham also said there should have been repercussions for former Fever guard and Amazon Prime commentator Sydney Colson, as well as fellow Amazon analyst Theresa Plaisance, who left their courtside seats to insert themselves in the altercation. "There's definitely a double standard," Cunningham stated. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! As for her feelings about whether her and her team wanted Wilson to play, while waiting for the league to announce if they would punish the Aces' star, Cunningham cleared the air saying, "We wanted her to play. I think that makes for good basketball." "Who would've thought that someone pointing would cause so many people to go into a mental spiral? That says a lot more about your mental status to anything the fans are doing," Cunningham said in response to both Wilson and viewers upset over her poking fun at the situation on TikTok. Cunningham and her co-host also spent a few minutes comparing the Game 2 incident involving Wilson and the fan with an Aces fan who stepped onto the court and pointed at Lexie Hull following a controversial foul call in Game 3. She tells it like it is, without apology. We need more athletes like her. While her teammate Raven Johnson apologized to A’ja Wilson on Friday via X for comments perceived as insensitive during a media appearance with Myisha Hines-Allen about Hines-Allen’s altercation and hard foul on Wilson, Cunningham stands firm in her beliefs and feels no need to bow to the WNBA establishment, which includes Wilson.

articles.title: Harden bendice a Hezonja: "Es muy bueno y aporta algo que no teníamos”.
articles.standfirst: 'La Barba' se deshace en elogios hacia el exmadridista, del que espera que sea importante en los Cavaliers
articles.summary: 'La Barba' se deshace en elogios hacia el exmadridista, del que espera que sea importante en los Cavaliers
articles.body: James Harden ya tiene claro quién puede ser una de las grandes piezas de los Cavaliers esta temporada. En el cierre del ‘training camp’ en Málaga, el veterano escolta se deshizo en elogios hacia Mario Hezonja, uno de los fichajes llamados a ganar protagonismo en Cleveland. “Mario Hezonja es muy bueno. Aporta algo a nuestro equipo que no teníamos”, sentenció. Harden fue todavía más lejos al desgranar todo lo que el croata puede ofrecer a los Cavaliers. “Es muy fuerte y físico. Puede tirar, pasar, finalizar cerca del aro y atacar hacia canasta”. Un perfil completo que, a ojos de una de las grandes estrellas de la NBA, puede darle al equipo algo que no tenía hasta ahora. Y el mensaje final de Harden deja clara la expectativa que existe en Cleveland con Hezonja: “Hoy se le ha visto realmente bien. Espero que sea muy importante para nosotros esta temporada”. El croata, que afronta un nuevo reto en la NBA, recibe así el respaldo público de uno de los pesos pesados del vestuario antes incluso de que eche a rodar la temporada. Hezonja, por su parte, no esconde su ambición. “La confianza del entrenador ya la tengo, por eso me han fichado”, explicó el jugador, que tiene claro cómo debe afrontar el desafío: “Voy a tope en cada entrenamiento y en cada partido”. Una mentalidad que considera imprescindible para llegar preparado al máximo nivel y a los ‘playoffs’. Su objetivo va más allá de encontrar un hueco en la rotación. “Quiero ser una pieza muy importante que contribuya a que el equipo gane”, afirmó. Y dejó claro que llega dispuesto a integrarse en una estructura ya consolidada: “Ya existe una identidad clara en la forma de jugar y quiero aportar y sumar a eso”. Donovan Mitchell también se marcha de Málaga con un recuerdo especial. El jugador, que ya ha visitado la ciudad en cuatro ocasiones, destacó la conexión con los aficionados y, especialmente, con los niños: “Ver a los niños con mi camiseta es increíble”. Para él, ese vínculo representa una de las razones que explican su pasión por el baloncesto. Y José Manuel Calderón puso el broche a una semana que los Cavaliers consideran un éxito. “Nos vamos muy contentos. Toda la organización está feliz de cómo ha transcurrido la semana”, aseguró el ‘assistant general manager’. Cleveland ya mira hacia el siguiente paso: el viernes, ante Boston, llegará el primer partido de pretemporada y la primera oportunidad de comprobar sobre la pista todo lo construido en Málaga.

articles.title: Valkyries' Janelle Salaun Wins 2026 WNBA Sixth Player Award, Full Voting Results
articles.summary: Golden State Valkyries forward Janelle Salaün was the unanimous pick for Sixth Player of the Year after setting multiple records off the bench.
articles.body:
Golden State Valkyries forward Janelle Salaün was the unanimous pick for Sixth Player of the Year after setting multiple records off the bench.

Salaün averaged 12.7 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 40 appearances. She had the most points (509) and made three-pointers (93) in a single season for a reserve player.

The 25-year-old was a regular starter for Golden State in its inaugural season, and she proved her value as the team went on to make the playoffs. The frontcourt grew a little more crowded, though, with the offseason additions of Gabby Williams and Kiah Stokes.

To accommodate the two vets, Salaün moved into a bench role and made a seamless transition. Her scoring average improved despite playing fewer minutes, and she was a more efficient shooter (42.5 percent overall and 39.2 percent on three-pointers).

"Whether she starts or she comes off the bench, it doesn't matter," coach Natalie Nakase told Marisa Ingemi of The IX Sports. "I'm still gonna have a fighter who wants to kill the other opponent, and she'll exhaust her minutes."

Williams, a two-time All-Star and the runner-up for Defensive Player of the Year, probably gets the most credit of any Valkyries player for their nine-win improvement.

Salaün is more indicative of why Golden State has been so successful in its first two years. The franchise has made a point to target international players, and the coaching staff has maximized the talent at its disposal.

Some might've scoffed at team governor Joe Lacob's goal of winning a championship within five years. It doesn't look so outlandish now.

articles.body: Sometimes, being at an Ivy League institution matters. articles.title: Pablo Laso respira: El Efes le ficha un base NBA tras romperse Mike James
articles.standfirst: Cameron Payne, ex de Thunder, Bulls, Cavs, Suns, Bucks, Sixers y Knicks, firma hasta final de temporada
articles.summary: Cameron Payne, ex de Thunder, Bulls, Cavs, Suns, Bucks, Sixers y Knicks, firma hasta final de temporada
articles.body: El Anadolu Efes mueve ficha ante el golpe más duro. La grave lesión en el tendón de Aquiles de Mike James, que le apartará de las pistas durante toda la temporada, ha obligado al conjunto turco a acudir al mercado y la respuesta ya tiene nombre: Cameron Payne. El base estadounidense, de 32 años, firma hasta el final de la temporada 2026-27 y aterriza en Estambul con la misión de cubrir un vacío de enorme calibre. No será una tarea sencilla. Mike James era una de las grandes referencias ofensivas del proyecto y su ausencia obliga al Efes a buscar alternativas para mantener el pulso en una temporada de máxima exigencia. Para minimizar el impacto, el club turco apuesta por un jugador que conoce el baloncesto europeo y que, además, acumula una larga experiencia en la NBA. Payne viene de jugar en el Partizan, por lo que no necesita descubrir ni la Euroliga ni la exigencia del baloncesto continental. Su currículum también pesa. Elegido en el número 14 del Draft de 2015 por los Oklahoma City Thunder, Payne pasó por Bulls, Cavaliers, Suns, Bucks, 76ers y Knicks. En Phoenix vivió además uno de los momentos más importantes de su carrera, formando parte del equipo que alcanzó las Finales de la NBA en 2021. Un recorrido que aporta experiencia, carácter y capacidad para asumir responsabilidades cuando el balón quema. Ahora le toca dar un paso al frente en Estambul. El Efes no busca únicamente un parche, sino una respuesta competitiva a una baja que cambia sus planes de temporada. Payne deberá hacerse rápidamente con los mandos del equipo, generar juego, aportar puntos y, sobre todo, asumir parte del liderazgo que deja vacante James. Su conocimiento reciente del baloncesto europeo juega a su favor en una adaptación que deberá ser prácticamente inmediata. El movimiento, además, mira más allá de la emergencia. El contrato hasta 2026-27 demuestra que el Efes ve en Payne algo más que un sustituto temporal. La lesión de James ha acelerado una decisión que puede terminar convirtiéndose en una pieza estable del proyecto de Estambul. Payne llega para apagar un incendio, pero con la oportunidad de quedarse mucho más tiempo del previsto en el corazón del nuevo Efes.

articles.title: El Valencia quiebra la resistencia maña en el último cuarto
articles.standfirst: Shorts (21+2+5), Mirotic (17+5) y Puerto (16) comandan la victoria taronja ante un buen Casademont Zaragoza
articles.summary: Shorts (21+2+5), Mirotic (17+5) y Puerto (16) comandan la victoria taronja ante un buen Casademont Zaragoza
articles.body: El esprint final del Valencia Basket, con un parcial de 15-31 en el último cuarto, desbordó por completo al Casademont Zaragoza y le permitió sumar en el Príncipe Felipe su primera victoria en la Liga Endesa 2026-27 en la segunda jornada del campeonato. Con un sólido dominio del rebote, gracias al trabajo de Gabriel Olaseni, y guiado por un gran Guillem Vives, el Zaragoza controló el choque en la primera mitad y con los puntos de Justin Jaworski aguantó el primer tirón del Valencia Basket, pero los visitantes, que se habían sostenido gracias a TJ Shorts, sumaron a Nikola Mirotic y a Josep Puerto y, de tres en tres, se llevaron el triunfo pese a entrar uno abajo al último parcial. Con Tray Bell-Haynes a los mandos y el control de los rechaces en ambos aros, el Casademont Zaragoza se hizo con el dominio del marcador y de las sensaciones en el inicio del choque. El base abrió en canal la defensa del Valencia y su equipo sacó partido de su lectura y de su verticalidad con dos triples de Jaworski y otros dos de Miguel González (18-9, m.6). Con una doble jornada de Euroliga por medio, el Valencia había tenido mucho menos tiempo para preparar el choque y se notó. Sus jugadores tenían que generarse sus propios tiros y, ante el riesgo de perder el tren del partido, Xavi Albert tuvo que acelerar el regreso a la pista del escurridizo TJ Shorts. Su presencia, y la de un sólido Neal Sako, animó a los suyos a apretar atrás para poder correr e igualar el choque (22-21, m.10). La agresividad defensiva en primera línea de Caleb Homesley mantuvo en pie a los locales, pero el Valencia, con Álvaro Cárdenas, empezó a circular mejor la pelota y acabó por ponerse por delante en una fase del partido en la que ambos equipos encadenaron fallos en la ejecución. El técnico local, Gonzalo García de Vitoria, echó mano de Guillem Vives, que se había cargado muy rápido, para retomar el control del ritmo; de Nico Brussino para volver a ver grande el aro; y de Gabriel Olaseni para volver a dominar con contundencia el rebote. Con ese tridente, el Casademont llegó arriba al descanso (39-36, m.20). Tras la reanudación, una exhibición de calidad de Nikola Mirotic puso por delante de nuevo al Valencia, pero el también veterano Vives no se achantó y mantuvo el pulso con determinación, bien secundado de nuevo por Brussino (57-57, m.27). articles.title: Kelsey Mitchell’s Caitlin Clark comments deserve context, including the benefits of all that attention
articles.summary: Kelsey Mitchell's WNBA salary jumped from under $60,000 to $1.4 million, but her press conference focused on the toll of playing with Caitlin Clark.
articles.body: Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell spent part of her season-ending press conference explaining what it’s like to play alongside Caitlin Clark. She talked about nasty online messages, the attention that follows the Fever and how difficult some days have become. "I don’t think people really understand how much we endure, man," Mitchell said Saturday. Later, she asked people to give the players "grace." Some coverage quickly turned that into Mitchell taking a shot at the Fever fanbase. I don’t think that’s an accurate reading of what she said. Mitchell has publicly praised Clark in the past and acknowledged the opportunities she helped create. She’s also allowed to explain what’s difficult about being her teammate. Neither makes her an enemy of the woman playing beside her. WNBA FIGHT OVER MALES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS EXPOSES HOW THE LEFT KEEPS ANSWERING A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED But the benefits of all that attention still belong in this discussion. Mitchell’s salary went from under $60,000 in 2020 to $206,000 in the season before Clark arrived in the WNBA to $1.4 million in 2026. That’s a pretty substantial part of the Caitlin Clark experience, too. Mitchell didn’t single out Fever fans Mitchell discussed getting "a lot of flak" for "being on her team," referring to Clark. She also referenced people throughout the basketball world and spoke positively about the Fever organization, praising it as "unbelievable." I read that as a broader description of the scrutiny that comes with playing alongside Clark. Her answer didn’t establish whether the criticism came from Fever fans, Clark’s detractors or some combination of the two. Those people exist, obviously, and being associated with the league’s biggest star makes Mitchell a target for their criticism, too. That’s different from declaring that Indiana’s own fans are the problem. Mitchell didn’t identify everyone sending her messages, and we shouldn’t fill in those blanks just because one interpretation makes for a more inflammatory headline. For example, The New York Times-owned Athletic ran the headline: "Kelsey Mitchell counters Fever GM’s defense of fans, vows to ‘be selfish’ in free agency." There’s one problem: None of Mitchell’s quotes in the story identifies Fever fans as the people she’s criticizing. Mitchell played six WNBA seasons before Clark arrived; her professional career didn’t begin when the rest of the country started watching the Fever. She’s experienced a version of this franchise that most of its current audience never saw. So, yes, I’m interested in hearing her describe what changed. That’s a worthwhile subject for reporters to explore. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! And Mitchell has described the positive changes. In a recent SLAM interview, she credited Clark and Angel Reese with creating opportunities for players throughout the league. "When Angel Reese and CC came in, it opened up so many doors for us: resources, financial, all of it," Mitchell said. ANGEL REESE’S LATEST WNBA CONTROVERSY SHOWS HOW VICTIMHOOD BECAME CENTRAL TO HER BRAND Mitchell explicitly recognized the financial benefits, and portraying her as someone who refuses to acknowledge them would be wrong. Mitchell’s experience is worth covering Jason Whitlock raised a worthwhile point on X while discussing Mitchell and teammate Aliyah Boston. "Their complaint is the media only covers one aspect of the Caitlin Clark experience," Whitlock wrote. He also argued the two Fever players "have every right to explain their experience playing in the shadow of Caitlin Clark." Mitchell’s perspective belongs in the coverage, and reporters should be interested in what she says, particularly given how long she’s been in Indiana. Where I’d push back is the idea that discussing the benefits amounts to telling her to shut up. Asking players to keep the upside in perspective doesn’t prevent them from explaining the downside. And explaining the downside doesn’t mean the rest of us have to agree with every conclusion they draw from it. For example, Mitchell described the difficulty of competing for fans who might not like her. But having fans dislike you is a fairly standard part of the athlete experience. They don’t have to appreciate your effort or acknowledge that you’re doing your best because they want you to fail. My main complaint with many WNBA players is that they often act like the unpleasant parts of being a public figure are something uniquely unfair to them. They aren't. I'm not a professional athlete, nor am I a very recognizable figure. But even I've received plenty of online hate for doing my job. It comes with the territory, and the same attention that helps drive bigger paychecks also brings more criticism. That's the tradeoff and most people happily make that deal. The bigger paycheck is part of the story Spotrac lists Kelsey Mitchell's WNBA cash earnings from 2018 through 2025 at $1,122,442. Her $1.4 million salary this season exceeded what she earned over those first eight seasons combined, and she's in position for another seven-figure contract in free agency this offseason. Mitchell’s performance earned her a maximum contract. The new collective bargaining agreement made that maximum much more valuable, raising it to $1.4 million as part of an enormous increase in player compensation. The previous maximum was around $250,000 per year. Clark’s ability to attract viewers is central to the league’s growing business. ESPN and ABC aired five WNBA regular-season games that averaged more than 2 million viewers this year, and all five featured Indiana. CBS, NBC, ION and Prime Video also drew their biggest regular-season WNBA audiences for Fever games. PRIME VIDEO WNBA BROADCAST CREW EMBARRASSES ITSELF WITH COVERAGE OF A'JA WILSON FAN INCIDENT Then Thursday’s season-ending game against Las Vegas averaged 2.25 million viewers across USA Network and CNBC, making it the second-most-watched WNBA first-round playoff game ever. Can you guess who played in the most-watched first-round game ever? Yeah, it was Clark and the Fever against the Connecticut Sun in 2024. The point is simple: Clark's massive audience has value, and the players are benefiting from it. And that’s where I still have a problem with the way this subject gets discussed around the league. The negative attention regularly becomes the main story, while the benefits get left out. I think that’s often because those benefits point to a story many WNBA players and media members don’t want to tell: a White girl from Iowa is driving the league’s popularity spike. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Getting obnoxious DMs from online trolls is part of the experience. But so is earning more in one season than you earned in the previous eight. Letting the first part dominate how you describe the whole thing gives the trolls an awful lot of influence. Mitchell isn’t nearly the worst example of that attitude. But Saturday’s answer still fit a familiar pattern of emphasizing what players have to endure without spending much time on what they’ve gained. Courtney Williams offered some useful advice last year Last year, Minnesota Lynx guard Courtney Williams gave what I thought was perfect advice for dealing with online hate. "Press the block button, bro. Press the block button and then move on," Williams said. Then came her most important comment: "We wanted more eyes on the game... So let’s embrace it." Credit to Williams for having the guts to say it. It's unfortunate that many of her colleagues didn't seem to heed her advice. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Mitchell has acknowledged the good that came with Clark’s arrival, and she deserves credit for that. But Saturday, she spent a lot of time explaining what she has to endure as Clark’s teammate. If we’re going to tell the full story of Mitchell’s experience, what she’s gained from all that attention belongs in it, too. That includes the $1.4 million paycheck.

articles.title: Jalen Duren Calls Out 'False' Rumors from Contentious Contract Talks with Pistons After Trade Buzz
articles.summary: Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren is hoping to put the rumors surrounding his contract dispute to rest.
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren is hoping to put the rumors surrounding his contract dispute to rest.

While speaking to reporters on Sunday after signing a five-year, $200 million contract extension, Duren called out the media for the ongoing speculation surrounding his contract negotiations. The Athletic's Sam Amick had reported in June that the big man was considering seeking a sign-and-trade away from Detroit after being "underwhelmed" by the team's initial offer.

"Nothing came from me. Everything that was being heard was speculation… That's part of the media's job… I don't fault anybody for that," Duren said Sunday. "I do know that a lot of the things were false, and people believe things without it coming from the source's mouth."

Amick and The Athletic's Hunter Patterson reported last week that the Pistons also caused friction with Duren when they included a mandatory monthly weight check-in in their initial version of the $200 million offer before rescinding the clause. Amick also reported that Pistons owner Tom Gores helped smooth things over when he "made a promise to Duren and his family that he would help provide a more positive Pistons experience" that served as "at minimum, an acknowledgement that this sensitive situation had gone sideways."

Duren became a restricted free agent at the end of a career year in which he averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds and earned his first All-Star selection. He was eligible for a max offer of $287 million over five years, but Detroit's offer fell well below that number after his disappointing playoff performance. His scoring average dropped to just 10.5 points as the Pistons lost in the Eastern Conference Semifinals.

The 22-year-old admitted that he needed to do some self-reflection after his lackluster postseason showing.

"It was humbling, I just need to get better," Duren told reporters when asked his biggest takeaway from how he ended the year. "… I'm man enough to acknowledge my flaws, and I'm man enough to acknowledge I'm not perfect. I'm also man enough to get my ass in the gym and work on those things."

It sounds like Duren has the right mindset as he tries to move forward with the Pistons and help them contend for a title this season.

"I am a Detroit Piston, I want to be a Detroit Piston for life," he said . "I want to give everything I've got for this city and the fans. From me to y'all, y'all will have everything I have. Y'all will get everything I can give."

articles.title: Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase will wear heart monitor following collapse
articles.summary: Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase spoke to reporters on Sunday for the first time following her collapse on Friday.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO ― Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase held a pregame press conference to address her collapse late in the fourth quarter of her team's Game 3 win over the Dallas Wings in the first round of the WNBA playoffs on Oct. 2.

Nakase told reporters on Sunday that she experienced "a little exhaustion." She got checked by doctors and said she will wear a heart monitor to gather information.

"Thank you guys obviously for your concerns and everything. I'm good," she said. "I think I talked to you guys about that, I wanted to learn from my father. He was an extremely hard-working man. I follow in his footsteps and I thrive in that.

"He just said, 'Do not let your career ever get involved in your mental health or your health gets complicated.' So when that happened, it definitely was like a wake-up call for me. I got checked through doctors to see if everything looks good."

During a timeout, Nakase was talking to a official and fell to the floor. She immediately received attention from assistant coaches and medical staff who helped her back to her feet and walked her to the bench where she continued to draw plays and coach the team.

Liberty, Dream and Aces, Valkyries in WNBA semifinal playoff action

Following the game, Valkyries assistant coach Kasib Powell and guards Tiffany Hayes and Gabby Williams told reporters that Nakase was OK.

Nakase said she didn't do anything differently. She ate and was well-hydrated going into the game on Friday. Nakase said she plans to be more discipline in taking care of own health, following her brief collapse.

"You know what I'm gonna do that my dad didn't do (and may he rest in peace) I'm gonna be proactive," Nakase said. "I think information for me is important and so I'm going to look to wear a heart monitor, just for information, just to see. You know, I have this Oura ring. But I just wanna be proactive, be smart. I understand this job for me, I love it. Sometimes I love it too much to a point where I overwork and I just wanna make sure I'm being smart."

Nakase drew concern from many including Las Vegas Aces head coach Becky Hammon, who has a good relationship with Nakase from when she coached under Hammon as an assistant coach in Las Vegas.

"That was kind of scary actually to to watch," Hammon told reporters on Sunday before their semifinals Game 1 matchup. "That little sucker popped right back up. Right back up onto that marker and kept it pushing so she's tough."
